One equation.

Watch a wave travel. See numerical diffusion, dispersion, and instability emerge as you change the Courant number.

LINEAR CONVECTION

∂u/∂t + a ∂u/∂x = 0

C = a Δt / Δx · u(x,t) = u₀(x − at)
Periodic domain x ∈ [0, 2) · constant wave speed

WHAT ARE WE SOLVING?

Carry a profile. Keep its shape.

Imagine a dye concentration carried around a loop by a uniform flow. The value u travels at speed a, with no physical diffusion: the exact solution simply translates the starting profile.

→distance = at = 0.6every feature moves equally

Same height. Same width. Here the pulse value is 2 and the background value is 1. Both fronts move 0.6 units to the right; nothing spreads or grows.

Connected ends. After a feature passes x = 2, it returns at x = 0. Negative velocity reverses the direction.

The numerical question. Can a grid-based method carry this profile accurately? The experiments below reveal artificial smearing, ripples, and unstable growth.

Illustration: square pulse, a = 1, t = 0.6 on x ∈ [0,2). This fixed example introduces the problem; the controls below set the live experiment.

02 Why it grows, or doesn’t

Von Neumann stability analysis

HOMEWORK INVESTIGATION

What stability condition does this method require?

The analytical amplification plot, stability verdict, and predicted growth curve are withheld. Use the numerical solution and measured perturbation history to gather evidence, then derive and justify your own condition from the update equation.

Amplification across wavelengths

Every Fourier mode must remain bounded. The dashed line is |G| = 1; leapfrog shows both roots.

A tiny perturbation, evolved directly

Solid: measured Fourier-mode amplitude. Dashed: ερⁿ (a spectral guide for leapfrog, which has two roots).

The root test sets δ¹ = 0 independently of δ⁰. At C = 1 and k = N/4 it exposes linear endpoint growth; use N divisible by 4 for this exact mode.

θ = 2πk/N. Perturbations evolve separately, avoiding subtraction cancellation at machine precision. This models error propagation; it does not measure newly injected round-off.

MethodOrder (time / space)Amplification relationStability requirementWhat to observe

Why leapfrog needs special care

Its two roots satisfy G² + 2iC sinθ G − 1 = 0. For |C| < 1 they are distinct and lie on the unit circle. One is a computational mode. We use one Lax–Wendroff step to start the method, with no time filter.

At |C| = 1 and |sinθ| = 1 the roots coincide. A generic perturbation of the two time levels can grow as nGⁿ even though |G| = 1. The usual CFL bound is |C| ≤ 1, but the robust root condition requires |C| < 1. Compatible startup may hide this endpoint defect.

What “implicit” means here

BTCS uses backward Euler in time and a centered derivative at the new time level. It solves a coupled periodic linear system on every step. This lab solves the periodic tridiagonal system, including its corner couplings.

Its amplification factor and stability condition are a homework investigation. Substitute a Fourier mode into the update equation, derive G(θ), and determine the requirements for all wavelengths. Compare your derivation with experiments.

Lax–Wendroff and MacCormack

For this linear constant-speed equation, the forward predictor and backward corrector in MacCormack reduce algebraically to Lax–Wendroff. Their curves should overlap to floating-point precision.

Both are second order and stable for |C| ≤ 1, yet dispersive ripples can occur near sharp fronts. Bounded oscillation is different from exponential instability.
